text:
Person: Start the washing machine and tell me when it's done.
Assistant: Sure. Which cycle should I use, cotton or quick wash?
Person: Quick wash, please. The baby will sleep soon and I want the noise to stop by then.
Assistant: A quick wash takes thirty minutes. Do you want me to run the dryer after that?
Person: Yes, and set a reminder to fold the towels. I also spilled cheese sauce on my shirt, so can you scrub it out for me?
Assistant: I can't scrub it myself, sorry. I can remind you to soak the shirt in cold water before the next wash.
Person: Okay, please do that for tonight at seven.

Someone wants the sprinklers to wave back and forth and water the garden, including the sour lemon tree and the seedlings no bigger than a coin.
water the garden
turn on the sprinklers
start teh sprinklers pls
the lawn looks dry, can you give it a drink
my lemon tree needs a good soak this morning
run the sprinklers for twenty minutes
i forgot to water the plants again, can you do it now
Could you please switch on the garden sprinklers? We are going away this weekend and I want everything wet first.

A television is for watching shows, news and films. Most people keep it in the living room, but some put a small one on a desk in the kitchen. The remote control lets you change many things. You can change the channel, make the sound louder or quieter, or mute it when the phone rings. Subtitles help when a show is noisy or the actors talk fast. People say turn on the subtitles, or switch to the cooking channel. If a spicy recipe goes by too fast, they say go back ten seconds. With streaming, you can also say pause, skip ahead, or play the next episode.

Ayita was a retired teacher who liked to drive to the market early. On the evening of the twelfth of March, the light in her garage was dim, and she could not read the little tyre gauge. She put her shopping bag down and spoke to her phone. 'Check my tyre pressure,' she said. The phone looked at the car's sensors and told her the front left tyre was a bit low. 'Please notify me tomorrow at eight to put air in it,' said Ayita. The assistant set a reminder for eight in the morning and said it was saved. Ayita smiled, locked the garage and went inside for tea.

name: descale_reminder
does: Tells you when to clean a kettle or coffee machine, with gentle tips such as using a soft toothbrush on the edges, so white scale doesn't build up and snow into your cup.
inputs: which appliance it is, and how often you use it
people say:
- there's white stuff inside my kettle
- my coffee tastes strange lately
- when should I clean the coffee machine
- remind me every month to descale the kettle
- how do I get the crusty bits out of the water tank

Tala did not know much about her phone, but she wanted to write to a new friend in Brazil. She held the phone close and said, 'How do I say good morning in Portuguese?' The assistant answered with the words and said them out loud. Tala wondered if she could spell them right, so she said, 'I don't want the long answer, just show me the letters.' The assistant wrote bom dia on the screen. 'Please double the size so I can read it,' she said. The assistant made the letters bigger. Then Tala asked it to save the words in her notes, and she added her friend as a new contact too.

Thabo sold potatoes and onions from a small shop near the bus stop. It was a bitter cold morning, and his hands were full of boxes. He spoke to the voice assistant on his phone. 'Add Mrs Dlamini to my contacts with the number 555 0142, and clear the old number for Mr Kumar,' he said. The assistant made a new contact for Mrs Dlamini and saved the number. Then it removed the old number from Mr Kumar's page and said both changes were done. Thabo nodded, set the last box of potatoes on the counter and turned the sign on the door to open.

Keoni worked as a cook, and on a windy morning he woke up with a sore throat. He was stirring a pot of soup when he pointed at his phone on the counter and said, 'Remind me to take half a tablet of my medicine at noon, and again at six.' The assistant said it had set two reminders, one at noon for half a tablet and one at six. Keoni asked for something warm to drink too, so he said, 'Set a timer for four minutes, I'm making tea.' The timer started. He tasted the soup, felt a little better, and went on cooking.

Person: Hello dear. I would be so grateful if you could put my photo up for my family, because my sister lives far away and I owe her a picture.
Assistant: Of course. Which photo would you like to post?
Person: The one of the cake on the kitchen shelf.
Assistant: Found it. Should I post it for everyone, or only for your sister?
Person: Only her. Could you also make her pay me a visit?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't make anyone visit. I can send her a message asking if she can come soon.
Person: Yes, please do that.

Kenji got home after a long night shift at the hospital. His motorcycle was parked outside, and his coffee tasted sour because it had been sitting since midnight. He sat down and said to the assistant, 'Read me the guest wifi password.' Then he shook his head. 'No, wait, I mean the main network, not the guest one.' The assistant said the main password out loud, slowly. Kenji typed it into his laptop. 'Also, resume my download from before I left,' he said. The assistant restarted the paused download and told him it had twenty minutes left. Kenji drank his bad coffee and went to bed.

Bills are the payments a home must make each month, like electricity, water and rent. Each one has a due date, and paying late can cost extra. Some people keep paper bills in a jacket pocket and forget them. A perfect way to avoid that is to set a reminder, or to let the bank pay for you on the same day each month. People say remind me to pay the water bill on the fifth, or move the rent date to the first. If an app is locked, they unlock it with a fingerprint to see what is due. They can also ask how much the last electricity bill was.

Someone who cleans their solar panels with vinegar wants to see how much power the house uses and makes, and how often to check.
show my power use
how much electricity did we use today
is it half of what we used last week
Does my power use this week fit under the usual amount?
what did the panels make compared with yesterday
tell me if we use more than double the normal at night
can you check often and warn me if the number jumps
I would like a daily summary of how much power we used, so I can cut the bill by a third.

A restaurant is a place to eat food that someone else cooks. People often book a table before they go, so they don't wait. They can change the time, the day or the number of people. They say things like book a table for four at seven, or make it six people instead. Opening hours matter too, because a kitchen may close early. On a cloudy day, fewer people sit outside, so tables inside fill up first. Some places hide their prices until you ask, but most put the menu online. For takeaway, you say I want to order food to pick up at eight. Many people check the menu on their phone or watch before they leave.

Someone is about to return home and wants to know if anyone is at the front door.
who's at my door
show the front camera
my hands are full, so can you look at the door for me
It's a warm night and I left a window open, did the alarm go off?
I heard a noise outside, can you check the yard
there's a heavy box by the gate, I think, the weight of it is bothering me, is it still there
Could you please let me see the camera, because I'm walking back alone and feel a bit nervous?
anyone out front

Naoki was a retired teacher who worried about running out of his heart medicine. On a grey afternoon he picked up his phone and said, 'How long does it take to drive to the pharmacy on Mill Street?' The assistant said about twenty minutes, with a little traffic. 'Is there a quicker way?' asked Naoki. The assistant found a road that was half the distance, but it had works on it, so it said the first route was better. Naoki asked it to guide him by voice. In the car, it said, 'In two hundred metres, turn left. This is your final turn.' He pulled up outside the pharmacy right on time.

Milena was texting her friend when she remembered the cookies. She said to the kitchen speaker, 'Heat the oven to 180 so I can bake.' The speaker said it was heating the oven to 180 degrees. A minute later Milena frowned. 'Sorry, I meant 200, the recipe says hotter.' The speaker changed it to 200 and said it would tell her when it was ready. 'Also put cookies on my calendar for Saturday so I don't forget to bring them,' she said. The speaker added it to her calendar. Soon the oven beeped, and Milena slid the tray in.

Hodan was a retired teacher who found it hard to type on a small screen, so she spoke to her phone a lot. One afternoon she was in the garden when the phone buzzed. She tapped it and said, 'Voicemail.' The assistant played a message from her cousin Ayaan, who asked about Sunday lunch. Hodan smiled. 'Call him,' she said. The assistant rang Ayaan on speaker while she kept weeding. After the call the light on the porch was dim, so she said, 'Alert me at five about the pie.' The assistant set an alert for five, and Hodan went on pulling weeds.

Someone saw a recipe for a square cake on television and wants to double it.
double it
make it twice as big
I need this for ten people, not five
scale the recipe up to eight servings
please record the new amounts in my recipe notes
how much flour if I make two cakes
what are the amounts for a bigger square tin
Could you please work out new amounts for twice as many people? My whole family is coming over tomorrow and the recipe only feeds four.

Person: I need to wash my work shirts.
Assistant: Sure. How many shirts do you have, and how warm should the water be?
Person: About six. I wear the sharp white ones, so keep it cool.
Assistant: Cool wash for six shirts. Should I fill the machine halfway or all the way?
Person: Half is fine. Can you also make the detergent twice as strong?
Assistant: I can't change how strong the detergent is, sorry. I can add a second rinse if you like.
Person: Okay, add the rinse. Thanks.

name: beach_water_check
does: Automatically checks the water temperature and wave size at a beach and says if it is a good time to talk a swim, using data from the local beach network.
inputs: the name of the beach, and the time you want to go
people say:
- is it warm enough to swim today
- are the waves big at Sandy Cove
- can the kids go in the water at four
- how cold is the sea this morning
- is it safe to get in the water right now

When you order something online, you pick the item, the size and where it should go. The shop packs it and it travels to your door. Sizes matter a lot for clothes and furniture. A shelf might be a hundred and twenty centimeters wide, so people check that it fits. There is often a maximum weight or size for free delivery. People say ship it to my office instead, or send two instead of one. If something is wrong, they say I want to return this, or swap it for a bigger size. Many shops let you change the delivery day, and people ask for it to come on Friday.

Someone going to the cinema wants the house alarm on and the lights low while they are away.
turn on the alarm
arm the house
I'm off to the cinema, lock up for me
make sure the doors are shut before I go
switch on the alarm and leave one light on
set the alarm to be twice as sensitive tonight
Do you mind turning on the house alarm? I will be out for about three hours and I can't pay to have someone watch the place.

Measurements tell us how big, heavy, hot or far something is. Different places use different units. In one country a road sign shows miles, in another it shows kilometers. A cook may weigh flour in grams, while an old recipe says ounces. People say how many cups is this, or change it to centimeters. A tv size is shown in inches, so some shoppers ask what that is in centimeters. Athletes train with distance in meters, and a doctor may check a baby's weight in kilograms. Raw chicken must be cooked to a safe heat, and a recipe may give it in Celsius or Fahrenheit, so people ask for the other one.

Person: Lock the front door and open the garage.
Assistant: I can do both. Which garage door do you mean, the big one or the side one?
Person: The big one. I need to get my salad ingredients out of the car.
Assistant: Done. The front door is locked and the big garage door is opening.
Person: Lovely. Do you know who is at the back gate? I heard a knock.
Assistant: I can't see the back gate because there is no camera there. I can show you the front door camera.
Person: No, that's fine. I'll go and look myself.

Neighbours often help each other. If a pet gets lost, people put up a note or type a message on a local group page. Local events, like a street sale or a school fair, are shared the same way. If the noise at night is too loud, a person might knock and ask politely. People say post a note about my lost cat, or remind me about the street party on Saturday. A simple message is best: say what is lost, where, and a phone number. Someone with a bad knee may ask a neighbour to help carry bags. When a pet comes home, people say take the notice down.

name: room_cooler
does: Turns on the fan or air conditioning in a room until it reaches the heat you want, and tells you when the room is cool again.
inputs: which room, and the heat you want
people say:
- it's so hot in the bedroom
- I'm angry, it's boiling in here and I can't sleep
- cool down the living room to twenty degrees
- turn on the fan, the piano room is stuffy
- mow the lawn is hot work, make the house cooler when I get back

Someone wants to know how far they rode on their bike today.
how far did I ride
my legs are dead, how many kilometres was that
I think that was a heavy ride, what was the distance
what was my total for the week
how far have I gone since morning
I designed a new route yesterday, how long was it
I want to see the distance on my bike computer
Could you tell me how far I cycled today? I'm trying to beat last week.

Moshe drove a delivery van, and between jobs he sat in the car park waiting. His phone was slow. 'I don't want to pay for more data,' he said to the assistant. 'Is the wifi at this place working?' The assistant scanned for networks and found one called Depot Guest. The car park was silent, so he asked it to join. The assistant asked for the password. Moshe read it from a sign on the wall, and the phone connected. 'Tell my team I'm online,' he said. The assistant sent a short message to his team group. Moshe opened his map and checked the next stop.

Person: I want to tell everyone about my snowy garden tonight after dinner.
Assistant: That sounds nice. Where would you like to post it, and do you have a photo?
Person: I don't know. I've never smoked a post before, I mean made a post.
Assistant: No problem. I can help. Do you want to post on your family page?
Person: Yes. And I want to celebrate the first snow of the year.
Assistant: Great. Please take a photo, and I will post it tonight at eight with a message about the first snow.
Person: Thank you.

Karim worked at a desk next to a window that looked out at the highway. The air in the office felt dry and heavy, and the room was dim because the clouds were thick. He spoke to the speaker on his desk. 'Turn on the air purifier and speak to me when the air is clean,' he said. The speaker started the purifier on a medium setting. Twenty minutes later it said, 'The air is clean now.' Karim also asked it to switch on the humidifier and raise the light a little. The speaker did both. He took a deep breath and went back to his emails.

Person: Play my happy playlist for the shop this Saturday afternoon.
Assistant: I can do that. Which speaker should I use, the shop floor or the back room?
Person: The shop floor. Make it quiet enough that people can talk.
Assistant: Got it. I'll set it to low volume at one o'clock this Saturday.
Person: Good. The picture on the wall makes me think of home, so I like songs that make you smile and not cry.
Assistant: I'll avoid slow songs. I can't tell which songs make people cry, but I can skip any song you say.
Person: That works.

Person: I'm late. Find a parking spot near the office.
Assistant: Sure. Which office, and how long will you be there?
Person: Park Street. I park there every Monday at nine, and I'm away until noon.
Assistant: There is a lot two minutes away with a free bed of spaces by the side gate. Should I pay for three hours?
Person: Yes, and fill it up every Monday if you can.
Assistant: I can pay for today. I can't pay every Monday automatically, but I can remind you at eight forty-five.
Person: Fine, do that.

Budi was a student who was going to visit his aunt for a short trip. On a rainy evening he put on his black jacket and sat down to study, but then he remembered the hotel. He said to the assistant, 'Find a room for two nights starting Friday.' The assistant looked and found a small hotel near the station. 'Sorry, I mean three nights, not two,' said Budi. The assistant changed it to three nights and asked if he wanted breakfast. 'Yes, please,' he said. The assistant saved the booking details in his notes and told him check-in was after two in the afternoon.

Min-jun drove a taxi, and one morning he had to pick up a friend from the airport. He put a pot of coffee in his bag and sat in the car. He said to his phone, 'When does flight two seven nine land?' The assistant checked and said it would land at ten fifteen, which was twenty minutes away from the time he thought. 'Is it late?' he asked. 'No, it is on time,' the assistant said. 'Tell me when it lands, and when the gate is known,' said Min-jun. The assistant said it would. He finished his coffee and drove toward the airport.

Sunita was a retired teacher who felt scared of making mistakes with money. One quiet morning she spoke carefully to her phone. 'Could you please move two hundred dollars from my savings to my everyday account? I have to pull cash out for the plumber tomorrow, and I would like to have it ready.' The assistant said it had moved two hundred dollars between her own accounts and read out the new balances. Sunita smiled. 'Thank you,' she said. 'And remind me to take my shopping cart to the market at ten.' The assistant set the reminder, and she felt a lot calmer.

Person: Start the robot vacuum.
Assistant: Which room should it clean, the shop floor or the back office?
Person: The shop floor. Actually, no, the back office first, then the shop.
Assistant: Okay, back office first. The wide hallway comes after. Should it also change the filter reminder?
Person: Yes, I think the filter is full of dust from the luggage boxes.
Assistant: I can't change the filter myself, but I can set a reminder for you to do it tonight.
Person: Please do. Thanks.

Irina sat at her office desk. It was a loud afternoon, with phones ringing everywhere, and she had to get to the post office before it closed. She whispered to the assistant on her phone, 'My parcel needs to go out today, and I haven't got time to wait.' The assistant understood. It looked up the post office on Elm Road and said it closed at five thirty. It also found a note saying the queue was short at four. Irina asked it to design a quick route there and back, and it showed a short walk. She grabbed the parcel, left a message for her boss, and walked out toward the old cinema, where the post office was next door.

Someone wants a reminder to take their medicine, and to take it half as often as before.
remind me to take my pills
set a medicine alarm
I only need it twice a day now, not four times
email my doctor and ask if I can take half the dose
send a note to the top clinic about my headache
Can you tell me when to take my next tablet, and make it less often this week?
Please remind me every morning at eight, because I keep forgetting and my group nurse said it matters
ping me when it's time for my medicine

name: meeting_joiner
does: Opens a call link at the right time and makes sure the sound and camera are comfortable, so you can heat up the coffee and not miss the start.
inputs: the call link or the name of the meeting, and the time
people say:
- join my nine o'clock call
- hook me up to the team meeting
- I'm late, get me into the call
- open the link my boss sent
- start the video call with Priya

name: ride_log
does: Saves a bike ride with its distance and time, and can move a ride to a different day if you gave the wrong date, using a working record of each trip.
inputs: the date, the distance and how long the ride took
people say:
- I just got back from a ride, save it
- log twenty kilometres from this morning
- that ride was on Sunday, not Monday
- note that I rode for an hour today
- put my bike sheet up to date with yesterday's trip

Mehmet had just woken up, and his eyes were still half shut. The bank was far from his house, so he used his phone. 'What's my balance, and move fifty into my savings,' he said. The assistant read out the balance and said it had moved fifty from his everyday account to his savings. 'Tag that as rent money,' Mehmet added. The assistant put a tag on the move. Then he asked it to read the email from the bank. It said the message was about a new card and had nothing urgent. Mehmet nodded, got up and made breakfast.

Birthdays are days when people say happy birthday and give small gifts. A gift can be a toy, a book or a warm scarf. Some people like to save ideas all year, so they have a minimum worry when the day comes. Cards are sent a few days early so they arrive in time. Like the wind, dates can slip away, so many people ask a phone to remember them. They say remind me of Dad's birthday next week, or give me ideas for a gift for a ten-year-old. They might also say buy a card for Gran, or change the reminder to the day before.

name: door_watcher
does: Tells you when a camera or motion sensor sees someone near your home and can scan the last few minutes to show you the top moments.
inputs: which camera or door, and how far back to look
people say:
- did anyone come to the door while I was out
- show me the back yard for the last hour
- I think someone was by the gate, check it
- tell me if you see movement tonight
- I got an idea someone is outside, look at the cameras

Linh was a retired teacher who lived alone, and she was always careful about her house. On the first of May, her son was coming to stay, and she had to give him a way in. She said to the smart lock, 'Make a new code for my son, and keep it working until Sunday.' The lock created a new code and said it would stop working on Sunday evening. 'Increase the time on the old guest code by one day,' she added. The lock did that. Then she asked it to send the new code to her son as a message, and she put the paper document with the old one in the bin.

A flight has a time when it leaves and a time when it lands. At the airport, a board shows each flight and the gate number. Sometimes a flight is delayed, which means it leaves later than planned. A passenger who waits at home can check the board on their phone. People say when does my flight leave, or is it late. If the gate moves, they ask which gate now. Some people jog through the airport when the gate is far away. A deep breath helps if you worry. At home, people ask what time to leave for the airport, so they arrive about two hours before.

Person: Plan my lunches for the week, but no sensor stuff, I just want food.
Assistant: Okay. Do you eat meat, and do you have any foods you can't have?
Person: I eat everything. Wait, no, I'm trying no cheese this week.
Assistant: Got it, no cheese. Do you want packed lunches that are easy to carry on a snowy walk to school?
Person: Yes, cold stuff is fine.
Assistant: I'll make five easy lunches, from Monday to Friday, with no cheese.
Person: Cool. Can you send it to me tonight?
Assistant: Yes, I'll send it at eight.

Cooling means keeping a home from getting too hot. A fan moves air around the room, and an air conditioner makes the air itself colder. On an average summer day, many people only need a fan. When the heat is strong, they turn on the air conditioner. People say make it cooler, set it to twenty-two degrees, or turn it off at night. If a room is too cold, they say let it warm up a bit. Many people ask the assistant to turn the cooling on before they get home, for example by Thursday afternoon, so the house is already cool.

Hugo was not good with technology, but his daughter had shown him how to speak to his phone. On Friday morning he had to go to the dentist, and his car was in the garage. He said slowly, 'Please call me a taxi to take me to Baker Street on Friday morning at nine.' The assistant asked for his address, and Hugo told it. It booked a ride and said the car would be at the door at eight forty. Hugo wanted a receipt printed, so he asked for the printer at home to print it, and the assistant sent the page there. He waited inside until the taxi arrived. The driver rounded the corner on time.

Someone wants a bike route that is about seventy kilometres long and has no crispy, dried-out roads full of loose stones.
find me a long ride
plan a route of seventy kilometres
I hate hills, can you pick a flat way
my last number was sixty, I want a little more
give me a ride I can finish in four hours
something about seventy km from my front door
Could you please plan a ride of about seventy kilometres? I'm training for a race and I want to go a bit further than last week.

Many families make rules for screen time, bedtime and chores. A child may have thirty minutes of tablet time after homework. At bedtime, a parent might read a story or play a quiet one on a speaker. A digital timer can tell the child when time is up. Parents change the rules as kids grow, and they use words like give me ten more minutes, or move bedtime to eight thirty. On school days, someone has to do the school run, and people say remind me to pick up Sam at three, or move the chore list to Saturday. A simple list on the wall helps.
